summaries.demographer: David Mckethan is a 46-year-old married Black man living in Angier, North Carolina, with his wife Tonya and two children, Maya and Caleb (Q05, Q51, Q89). He has a high school diploma and some college, and he is currently enrolled part time in community college for business administration (Q90-Q92). His household rents, relies on two hourly incomes, and occupies a modest working-family position with stable employment but limited financial cushion (Q56-Q58, Q72-Q74, Q83). His life course reflects strong local rootedness, intergenerational family ties, church involvement, and gradual upward-mobility efforts (Q01, Q47, Q108).
summaries.behavioral_economist: David is loss-averse and budget-conscious, using notebooks, phone reminders, envelopes, and paycheck-based planning to manage uncertainty (Q17, Q18, Q61). He is willing to delay gratification by returning to school while working full time, but immediate family needs often take priority over long-term goals (Q02, Q62, Q108). His decisions are strongly shaped by household stability, peer respect, church norms, and his identity as a reliable provider (Q05, Q47, Q83). He avoids high-risk coping strategies, prefers small practical adjustments, and treats emergencies like car repairs as threats to family equilibrium (Q38-Q40, Q82).
summaries.political_scientist: David is a moderate but fairly consistent Democrat who votes most of the time and has become more attentive to local politics as a parent and longtime Angier resident (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). His civic orientation emphasizes public schools, health care, wages, fair policing, small business opportunity, and respect for rural Black communities (Q24, Q27, Q108). He supports Black Lives Matter's core concerns while engaging mainly through family, church, and community conversation rather than sustained protest activity (Q26-Q30). His institutional trust is mixed: he values voting and community institutions but is cautious about policing and politicians who appear only during campaign season (Q20, Q23, Q24).
summaries.psychologist: David presents as conscientious, relational, practical, and community-oriented, with a strong provider identity and a tendency toward worry under financial and scheduling pressure (Q43-Q45, Q83). He regulates emotion through prayer, music, basketball, planning, and talking with his wife or sister, though he still struggles with late-night rumination (Q44, Q45, Q50). His self-concept is built around dignity in work, family reliability, Black Southern cultural pride, and service to others (Q01, Q47, Q109). He is future-oriented but cautious, motivated by incremental progress rather than dramatic risk-taking (Q62, Q65, Q108).
